subject: Hawthorne Health — sudden AZ routing bifurcation causing 5xx and latency spikes
messages:
From: Ari Cohen <ari.cohen@hawthornehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hawthorne Health SRE <sre@hawthornehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production impact — sudden 5xx + latency at our east-us AZ

Team —

We're seeing a sudden widening of 5xx rates and tail latency for tokenization and embedding endpoints from our east-us AZ (us-east-az2). Impact started ~08:50 PT and is affecting ~30% of our traffic to Redwood. Reqs to the generation endpoint are often timing out at 15s.

Attached a short tail of client-side logs (client_kv_tail.log) and a traceroute that shows requests traversing an unexpected AZ hop. We haven't changed our config. Please advise immediate mitigation steps and whether you can route our traffic away from that AZ.

This is P0 for our morning batch jobs.

—Ari
CTO, Hawthorne Health

---
(Attachment: client_kv_tail.log — text/log, 28KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Cohen <ari.cohen@hawthornehealth.com>, Hawthorne Health SRE <sre@hawthornehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — sudden 5xx + latency at our east-us AZ

Ari / team —

Thanks for the rapid heads-up and the logs. We're looking. Initial signal from our telemetry: a routing bifurcation at the edge is sending ~28% of Hawthorne traffic to us-east-az2 where an intermediate NLB is reporting elevated queue depths and a backend pool cycling. Generations that hit that pool are seeing token-decode errors and long tail latency.

Immediate actions I'm triggering now:
- Canaries: pin a 100% canary for new routing off us-east-az2 to fallback pool (target us-east-az1) for Hawthorne only.
- Team: Marissa, please coordinate the tenant pin and confirm routing policy change.
- Grace: pull the NLB instance logs and health checks for the az2 backend pool; share any anomalies.
- Ari: can you confirm whether you have custom Source IP affinity or sticky sessions that we should be aware of?

I'll escalate to execs if we need priority capacity or credits.

Rafael
Director, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

I've queued the tenant-level routing override. Rolling to Hawthorne now — expected completion in ~3 minutes. I'll monitor QPS and 5xx rate post-roll. If traffic still lands in az2 after override, we'll force a regional steer at the edge (needs Sean to sign off for short-term capacity burst).

Quick status:
- Routing override triggered: tenant pin -> us-east-az1
- Health: Grace reports spike in NLB 502s and node oom patterns (attaching snippets).

I'll post a follow-up once the 5xx rate drops.

-Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — sudden 5xx + latency at our east-us AZ

FYI — logs from the az2 NLB/backend pool show:
- Repeated 502/524 from a subset of inference workers (same driver binary).
- Abrupt memory pressure events on 3 nodes just before the error window.
- No DNS changes on the customer's side; request paths inbound show expected tenant id.

Short-term mitigation: spinning up 6 warm workers in us-east-az1 and forcing steady-state allocations for Hawthorne. If that doesn't reduce customer-impact we'll request a managed burst in us-east-az1 from capacity ops.

Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Hawthorne impact — traffic steered, monitoring, and next steps

Ari —

Thanks again for the quick signal. Summary of actions taken and current status: 

What we did (timeline):
- 09:30 PT: Confirmed routing bifurcation; NLB/backend anomalies in us-east-az2.
- 09:33 PT: Tenant routing override applied (Marissa).
- 09:40 PT: Additional warm workers provisioned in us-east-az1 (Grace).
- 09:50 PT: Cross-AZ emergency steer authorized by Sean; traffic fully shifted off az2 by 09:54 PT.

Current status:
- 5xx rate for Hawthorne generation endpoints dropped from peak ~12% to ~0.6% of baseline.
- Tail latency p99 has normalized; p95 within SLA.
- We continue to monitor and will not revert traffic until backend pool in az2 is verified healthy by Ops.

Next steps / asks for you:
- Please confirm whether Hawthorne wants us to keep the steer for the overnight batch (we recommend keeping it until az2's backend pool is fully remediated).
- We'll share the incident note and a root-cause hypothesis once Equinox provides the node crash dump.

Again, apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with the post-incident summary and any credit reconciliations.

Rafael Mendes
Director, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
